events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph by boat.** I'd rate it **2 (average)**, the best of the four.
- **Fish 100-120+ ft of water.** Boats were working well beyond 120 ft there in early July.
- **Run spoons.** Spoons were the main producer at South Haven, and historical July reports at these ports also favor spoons.
- **Other ports:** South Haven **1 (below average)**. Grand Haven **2 (average), low confidence**, because its latest report is 27 days old. Muskegon **about 1, low confidence**, because I found no salmon report there since June 7.

## Why

- **St. Joseph has the best recent boat report:** the July 5 report rated boat salmon fishing average, with anglers working past 120 ft (St. Joseph, 2023-07-05).
- **South Haven was weaker:** its July 5 boat report was below average, with fish caught mainly around 100 ft and spoons producing most of the catch (South Haven, 2023-07-05).
- **Water is warm:** I'd expect the typical Chinook and coho range of 52-58 F to be found deeper offshore, since the buoys read about 71 F (St. Joseph and South Haven, today's conditions summary).
- **Similar past weeks were mostly slow to average:** when July surface water was near 71 F in earlier seasons, boat reports were mostly 0-1 with a few 2s (past seasons, 2022).

## Evidence

**Recent reports**
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-05, boat, 120+ ft, quality 2: "Boat anglers targeting salmon had decent fishing this week… mixed bag of fish… fishing well beyond 120 feet of water."
- South Haven, 2023-07-05, boat, 100 ft, spoons, quality 1: "Boat anglers were fishing very deep water and a few fish were also caught around 100 feet. Most fish were caught on spoons."
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21, boat, 65-160 ft, fish 35-90 ft down, quality 2: "Orange spoons worked well along with green or yellow meat rigs." This is 27 days old.
- Muskegon: the latest salmon report is 2023-06-07, 41 days old. Nothing in the last four weeks.

**Past seasons (similar ~71 F surface water, within 21 days of today)**
- Grand Haven, 2022-07-14, quality 0: "Salmon fishing was slow for boat anglers."
- Muskegon, 2022-08-03, quality 3: boats caught fish 65-130 ft down in 140-250 ft of water, with glow spoons and flies in low light.
- St. Joseph, 2022-07-20, quality 1: "a few fish around 100 feet of water."

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool was in backtest mode and returned live data as unavailable. Its summary for the week before 2023-07-18 gives buoy surface water of 71 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven, and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon.
- Upwelling winds in the last three days were light at all four ports (St. Joseph 4 h, South Haven 0 h, Grand Haven 0 h, Muskegon 1 h).
- The tool returned no modeled cold-layer depth, so I don't have a current depth for the 52-58 F water.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are 13 days old (St. Joseph and South Haven) and 27-41 days old elsewhere. The July 12 bulletin isn't in the database, so this is a guide, not current fishing.
- The current water temperatures are a backtest summary, not live readings. Check the latest buoy and cold-layer data before you go.
- Ratings for Grand Haven and Muskegon are low-confidence expectations, not findings from recent reports.
- Fish depth was not reported for St. Joseph or South Haven in July, so the 100-120 ft advice is based on where boats were working, not where fish were held.

## Sources

- St. Joseph and South Haven, 2023-07-05: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- Past-season comparisons: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31f444a, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31e454b, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf
